newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Rules agreed for NZ electricity market contracts.
newsitem.headline: Rules agreed for NZ electricity market contracts.

text.p: Rules were agreed on Thursday for the trading of New Zealand electrity market pricing contracts (EMPs), Peter Woodhouse, manager of electricity markets for brokers Harlow Butler said.
A set of legal rules by which signatories agree to settle financial contracts in the wholesale market was agreed after 18 months of development, he said.
"The success of a self-regulating secondary market depends on a level playing field and a market standard, such as EMPs, sets the platform," he said.
EMPs will be used as a tool to manage risk in the new wholesale electricity market. They can vary for periods varying from half an hour to 12 years.
Initial signatories ot the document were representatives of Pacific Energy Ltd of Auckland and PowerBuy Group Ltd, both buying groups established by energy companies.
PowerBuy Chief Executive Roger Taylor said EMP would provide standardisation that would help increase liquidity and encourage new entrants into the trading market.
